correctness.rationale: An exact determinant factorization via within-ring root-of-unity Vandermonde products and cross-ring binomial resultants reduces the 3n-dimensional problem to one three-point complex-distance product. For fixed phase difference, strict quadratic convexity forces reflection of the outer phases; strict logarithmic concavity in cos(theta) yields unique interior cosine or endpoint and the sharp critical radius t=2+sqrt(3). All positivity assumptions, n ranges and h>0 avoid degeneracies. Direct finite Gram computations supplement, not replace, the infinite-dimensional quantifier proof.

originality.rationale: Two primary research articles were read in HTML full text, and their stated sampling bounds were compared with the exact three-regular-orbit determinant theorem. Semantic searches of public mathematical records and relevant general-web literature did not reveal a stronger covering three-orbit angular classification. The archived two-ring normalized-evaluation result has one pairwise cross-distance term only, so does not logically determine the present product of three competing pairwise distances. Residual risk remains in older Fekete/logarithmic energy literature; the novelty assessment is best-knowledge, not a uniqueness certificate.
residual_risks: A classical theorem about three concentric circles, discrete logarithmic energy or Fekete products might imply this special constrained angular design; not exhaustively excluded.

value.rationale: A natural normalized sampling design with three equally populated rings displays a nontrivial, exact optimizer geometry phase transition at scale h~1/n. The threshold and two analytic determinant branches are independent of all positive radial monomial weights. This is structural information beyond the two-ring half-step rule and provides a meaningful exact design prescription, although unrestricted Fekete placement and condition-number minimization are not asserted.
